Calculate incidence from flusurvey data

Source: R/get_incidence.r
get_incidence.Rd

This calculates incidence according to a given column in the supplied data.

Usage

get_incidence(
  data,
  incidence.columns = "ili",
  aggregation = c("week", "day", "month", "year"),
  denominator = c("active.members", "reports"),
  min.N = 1,
  by = NULL
)

Arguments

data

a data table, usually generated by merge_data

incidence.columns

one or more columns which specificy incidence; default: "ili"

aggregation

the timescale of aggregation, by default "week"

denominator

what to use as denominator, active members or all reports in a week

min.N

the minimum denominator, by default 1

by

one or more variables by which to group

Value

a data.table with the incidence

Author

seb

Examples

dt <- extract_data(simulated_data, years = 2013:2014)
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use flag_ill_contacts().
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use flag_ill_contacts().
get_incidence(dt, incidence.columns = "ili", aggregation = "week")
